facts.statement: The extinct bird Pandanaris convexa was described in 1947 by the scientist Alden H. Miller.
facts.quote: described in 1947 by Alden H. Miller

facts.statement: Pandanaris convexa is the sole species within its genus, Pandanaris.
facts.quote: It is the only member of its genus, Pandanaris

facts.statement: The upper mandible of Pandanaris convexa measures 7.0 mm in length.
facts.quote: Pandanaris convexa has an upper mandible (7.0 mm in length)

facts.statement: The narial opening of Pandanaris convexa is approximately 30% larger than that of related extant cowbirds.
facts.quote: its narial opening is approximately 30% larger

facts.statement: Pandanaris convexa possesses a distinct even curvature on its culmen that is unique among icterids.
facts.quote: The species has a distinct "even" curvature of its culmen that is not found in any other icterid

facts.statement: Pandanaris lived from the Chibanian to the Late Pleistocene, between 0.21 and 0.0117 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Chibanian to Late Pleistocene (0.21 to 0.0117 million years ago)

facts.statement: The first fossil remains of Pandanaris were discovered at the La Brea Tar Pits in California.
facts.quote: The first remains were from the La Brea Tar Pits in California

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Pandanaris have also been found in Florida.
facts.quote: remains have also been found in Florida

facts.statement: Additional remains of Pandanaris were found at San Clemente de Térapa in the Mexican state of Sonora.
facts.quote: Other remains have also been found at San Clemente de Térapa in the Mexican state of Sonora

facts.statement: Based on fossil evidence, Pandanaris had a wide distribution across the Americas.
facts.quote: had a large distribution throughout the Americas

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Pandanaris likely co-evolved with Pleistocene megafauna.
facts.quote: the convex-billed cowbird likely co-evolved with Pleistocene megafauna

facts.statement: Pandanaris inhabited grassland habitats shaped by megafauna and fed on insects stirred up by their foraging.
facts.quote: inhabiting the grassland habitats that were shaped by these species and feeding on the insects that their foraging stirred up

facts.statement: It is debated whether Pandanaris went fully extinct because it was wholly dependent on megafaunal communities and could not tolerate altered habitats.
facts.quote: Pandanaris may have been so wholly dependent on megafaunal communities that it could not tolerate the altered habitats and went fully went extinct throughout its range
